hints.title: Branch Depth Accumulation
hints.text: The depth of a tree depends on the paths through its branches. How can knowing the maximum depth of each child subtree directly determine the depth of the parent node?

hints.title: Bottom-Up Height Recurrence
hints.text: The maximum depth of any node is 1 plus the maximum of the depths of its left and right subtrees.

hints.title: Post-Order Depth Calculation
hints.text: Base case: if the node is null, return 0. Compute the depth of the left subtree and the depth of the right subtree. Return 1 plus the larger of the two depths.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: number of nodes in tree (0 <= N <= 10^4)
H: height of tree (log N balanced, N skewed)
complexity.notes: Visits each node once in post-order. Call stack height equals the depth of the tree.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Generating all root-to-leaf paths explicitly requires extra memory and string/array copying taking O(N * H) time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Post-order divide and conquer computes subtree depths in a single bottom-up traversal taking O(N) time and O(H) auxiliary space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Handling null root cleanly returning 0, recursive recurrence 1 + max(left, right), awareness of recursion stack depth on skewed trees.
